summary:
France's government has suspended police use of stun grenades at high school demonstrations, it said on Wednesday, after a 15-year-old boy lost a hand in a clash with riot police. The interior minister rejected accusations of brutality, and nearly 460 schools were affected by continuing protests.

Kenya has confirmed its first Ebola case, a patient who passed through several cities in DR Congo, drove to Uganda and flew to Kenya. Ten people linked to the patient have been quarantined, and Nairobi Hospital says it remains open and safe. In Russia, a worker at a plague research institute in Siberia died on October 2, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny pneumonic plague caused the death, and the WHO says it does not know what the causative agent was.

Ukraine says Russia launched an overnight barrage of 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and ballistic missiles, killing at least 24 people. President Zelenskyy said a strike on a residential building in Pryluky killed four children. In Yemen, Houthi forces attacked Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and drones, and the UN says more than 200,000 people have been displaced.

headlines.title: France suspends police use of stun grenades at school protests
headlines.summary: France's government has suspended police use of stun grenades at high school demonstrations after a 15-year-old boy lost a hand in a clash with riot police. The interior minister rejected accusations of brutality, and nearly 460 schools were affected by continuing protests.

headlines.title: Kenya records its first Ebola case, with ten contacts quarantined
headlines.summary: Kenya has confirmed its first Ebola case, a patient who passed through several cities in DR Congo, drove to Uganda and flew to Kenya. Ten people linked to the patient have been quarantined, and Nairobi Hospital says it remains open and safe.

headlines.title: Russian authorities deny pneumonic plague caused lab worker's death
headlines.summary: A worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died on October 2, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Authorities deny pneumonic plague caused the death, and WHO says it does not know what the causative agent was.

headlines.title: Russian strikes kill at least 24 people across Ukraine
headlines.summary: Ukraine says Russia launched an overnight barrage of 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and ballistic missiles, killing at least 24 people. President Zelenskyy said a strike on a residential building in Pryluky killed four children, one of the most vile attacks by Moscow's army.

headlines.title: Houthi attacks hit Yemen's Aden airport and Saudi airports
headlines.summary: Houthi forces attacked Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones, Yemen's transport ministry said, as fighting with Saudi-backed forces intensified. Saudi Arabia says Houthi attacks on two of its airports killed three foreign nationals, and the UN says more than 200,000 people have been displaced.

headlines.title: Canada will not allow assisted dying for mental illness alone
headlines.summary: Canada's justice minister said on Wednesday that medically assisted suicide will not be allowed for people whose only condition is mental illness. The expansion, which had been due in March 2027, has been paused indefinitely.

headlines.title: Gaza lies in ruins three years after October 7 attacks
headlines.summary: Three years after the Hamas-led attacks in Israel, much of Gaza lies in ruins, and more than 74,000 people have been killed there. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take personal responsibility or order a state inquiry into the failures before the attacks.

headlines.title: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai win the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry
headlines.summary: Henri Kagan of France and Kenso Soai of Japan won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their work on asymmetric molecules, the award-giving body said on Wednesday. The prize is worth about $1.2 million and is shared between the two scientists.
